name: Daniel

timeline.note: Daniel's story spans from Nebuchadnezzar's first deportation (c. 605 BC) into the reign of Cyrus of Persia (c. 530s BC), but no personal birth or death year is given, so no specific date is plotted.

interpretive_note: Most evangelical scholars affirm the traditional sixth-century BC exilic dating implied by the book itself, but many critical scholars date the book of Daniel to the 2nd century BC on the basis of its detailed later-historical content and Aramaic/Hebrew style — a significant, long-running authorship and dating dispute worth noting rather than resolving silently.
source_summary: Judean noble exiled to Babylon who rose to prominence through God-given wisdom, survived being thrown into a den of lions for continuing to pray, and received sweeping visions of future kingdoms and a coming "son of man" — language Jesus later applied to Himself.
family_friendly_summary: Daniel was a young man taken far from home to live in Babylon, but he decided to stay faithful to God even in a strange new place, starting with what he chose to eat. God gave Daniel special wisdom, and he became famous for explaining dreams no one else could understand, including a king's dream about future kingdoms. Daniel's three friends were once thrown into a blazing furnace for refusing to worship an idol, and God protected them completely. Later, Daniel himself was thrown into a den of hungry lions simply for continuing to pray to God — but God shut the lions' mouths and kept him safe all night. Daniel's story is a wonderful example of staying faithful and brave even when it's difficult, and trusting that God is always with us.
adult_story: Daniel was among the young Judean nobles taken to Babylon after Nebuchadnezzar's first siege of Jerusalem, where he and three companions — renamed Belteshazzar, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego — resolved not to defile themselves with the king's food, and God gave them wisdom "ten times better" than all the royal magicians (Daniel 1). Daniel alone could recall and interpret Nebuchadnezzar's forgotten dream of a great statue representing successive kingdoms, struck down by a stone "cut out without hands" — a picture of God's eternal kingdom breaking into human history (Daniel 2). His three friends survived being thrown into a fiery furnace for refusing to worship Nebuchadnezzar's golden image, emerging without even the smell of smoke on them (Daniel 3). Decades later, under Belshazzar, Daniel alone could interpret mysterious handwriting on the palace wall announcing the kingdom's fall that night (Daniel 5). Under Darius the Mede, jealous officials tricked the king into banning prayer to anyone but himself; Daniel kept praying openly toward Jerusalem anyway and was thrown into a den of lions, but God shut the lions' mouths and he emerged unharmed (Daniel 6). Daniel also received visions of seventy "weeks" of years counting toward the Messiah's coming and being "cut off," and a coming "son of man" given everlasting dominion — language Jesus applied directly to Himself (Daniel 7:13-14; 9:24-27; Matthew 26:64).
devotionals: Daniel kept praying toward Jerusalem even with lions waiting for him. May God give us that same courage to stay faithful, whatever it costs us.
Daniel saw a 'son of man' given a kingdom that never ends — Jesus claimed that title for himself, and his kingdom is the one we belong to.
A stone cut without human hands shattered every earthly kingdom in Daniel's dream. Jesus's kingdom is the one built to never fall.
